data.turoyo: Koʕəfrənne gurtko naʕəmto qadar saḥnəke mede. I gurtkayo, kəmmila ḥawwe.
data.translation: Sie graben eine kleine Grube, ungefähr so groß wie ein kleiner Eßnapf. Die Grube nennen sie "Häuschen" eig." Unterkunft".

rationale: Thin Infectum cell: digging a small game pit supplies an explicit created object and unusual -nne sequence. Printed root retained despite inherited hearing warning.

“Soiled out from the rock” incorrectly suggests dirtying rather than excavation. The entry gloss is graben, and the preceding 94/17 example independently establishes digging around a stone slab; the personal-communication example describes extracting something from rock.

summary: The entry explicitly calls Ritter's root a Hörfehler. Preserve that editorial warning verbatim; the additional printed token is not independent confirmation that ʕfr is the speaker's actual root.
94/17 has b- instrument and a surrounding area;94/492 has a newly created pit object. Both fit the inherited graben sense.
The -nne before singular gurtko cannot straightforwardly be a coreferential plural patient. A benefactive analysis is plausible but unconfirmed.
The inherited Ilyas -wayna quotation establishes an Infectum-wa filing even though it was stored under Infectum. No new stem, sense or light-verb idiom is justified.
Confirm the root actually pronounced in Ritter94/17 and94/492, in light of the inherited Hörfehler warning; retain the source spelling until checked.
